effect: Calcium exposes grip sites so myosin can pull the filaments past each other; the fibre shortens without the filaments shortening. The remaining step appears to address relaxation.
reaction: The distinction between sliding and shortening is clear and satisfying.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and pumping calcium back into storage should help the fibre relax.
expectation: I expect the calcium-pumping membranes to remove calcium from around the filaments, allowing the fibre to relax.

effect: The result completes the cycle: ATP-powered pumps return calcium to storage, covering the grip sites and stopping the pull. An outside pull helps the fibre relax.
reaction: It was interesting that relaxation also requires cellular work.

mostWorthwhile.text: The calcium signal and shortening fibre were the most worthwhile: the result clearly explained how the filaments slide past each other without shortening.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the fibre scaffold and filling it with filaments felt somewhat repetitive; both steps were straightforward and offered only one combination.

surprise.text: ATP helps myosin release and reset, and it also powers calcium pumps during relaxation. That broadened my understanding of its role beyond pulling.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary, though combining the transporter-bearing cell with fibre structures produced a scaffold without explaining much about that transformation.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter: the progression from fuel to pulling and relaxation made me curious how the fibre connects to larger body systems, although several assembly steps were predictable.
